title: Man dies after two Taser hits in west Edmonton
article: A man is dead after being hit twice with a Taser at a pawnshop in Edmonton's Jasper Place neighbourhood.
The victim is identified as Trevor Ashley Grimolfson. He owned a north Edmonton tattoo parlour.
Police responded to a mischief call just after 11.00 AM Wednesday. They found a man threatening people and smashing windows at Dan's Pawnshop at 15347 Stony Plain Road.
Earlier that morning, witnesses saw an agitated man walking along Stony Plain Road, waving his arms and taking sideways steps.
'He was erratic,' said Norma Strelkov, who works at a nearby Thrift Store. 'He wasn't acting like any normal person would.'
Michelle Furoy was working at a liquor store across the street from the pawnshop when she saw DVDs being thrown out of the store.
'You could hear him screaming, he was destroying Dan's shop,' she said.
The noise continued after police officers arrived, she said. Furoy eventually saw Grimolfson being taken out of the pawnshop on a stretcher.

Officers deployed a Taser twice on the man, to no effect, said Edmonton police spokesman Jeff Wuite. He said Grimolfson came towards the officers. They wrestled him to the ground and put him in handcuffs. Grimolfson then lost consciousness, Wuite said.
The man was taken to the hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Staff at the shop Grimolfson owned were noticeably shaken, but unwilling to say anything about the incident.

The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) has taken over the investigation into Grimolfson's death since he died in police custody. ASIRT is an independent provincial department recently formed to investigate complaints of serious injury or death that may have resulted from the actions of officers. This is the first time it will look into a Taser-related death.

Clifton Purvis of ASIRT says, 'It could be any number of things totally separate from the deployment of the Taser (that caused Grimolfson's death). He may have had a pre-existing condition. He may have fallen and hit his head. I have no idea.'

Global News spoke to witnesses who saw Grimolfson in his final minutes. One witness, Sherri Shesky, says she's not questioning the actions of police, and that after seeing the way the man was behaving, 'I would have done it myself.'
Edmonton police officers began carrying Tasers in 2001. Out of the force's 1,400 officers, about 400 are currently trained to carry and use the devices.
